commit.message:
chore(claw-server-rust): remove unused auth_token sidecar config (#2730)

The Rust claw server parsed a sidecar auth.token into Config.auth_token, but
nothing produced, sent, or read it. The Chromium-authored sidecar config schema
has no auth field, so auth_token was always None; there is no auth middleware,
and the parallel bun server has no inbound token auth either. It was a scaffold
placeholder from the initial rust port. Remove the field, the SidecarAuth struct,
and its parsing rather than enforce a credential nothing sets. Inbound access
control for the MCP endpoint is loopback binding plus flags.allow_remote_in_mcp.

Fixes #2720

commit.message:
fix(browseros-mcp): stop token slice from infinite-looping on multibyte text (#2727)

slice_text_by_estimated_tokens binary-searched for the largest UTF-8 prefix
within a token budget, but when a midpoint fell inside a multibyte character
floor_char_boundary could floor back onto the current lower bound, making no
progress and spinning the loop forever. On large non-ASCII snapshots/diffs this
pinned a Tokio worker at 100% with no cancellation point, surviving session
death until a full restart (#2707).

Because estimate_text_tokens is exactly ceil(bytes / APPROX_CHARS_PER_TOKEN),
the largest prefix within budget is APPROX_CHARS_PER_TOKEN * max_tokens bytes;
compute that directly, clamp to the input length, and floor once to a char
boundary. This removes the loop entirely and returns identical output for every
input the search previously terminated on. A debug_assert guards the coupling to
the estimator, and tests cover the multibyte-termination case, two-byte text,
zero and over-budget inputs, and prefix maximality.

commit.message:
fix(server): survive log-write failures and bound log growth (#2726)

* fix(server): survive log-write failures and bound log growth

The pino console and file destinations had no error listener, so a failed write
on a full disk (ENOSPC) surfaced as an uncaught error and looped one failed
flush into a flood of captured events. Attach an error guard to both
destinations that degrades to stderr and keeps serving, so a write failure can
never crash or spam.

Log rotation ran only at startup and only by age, letting the file grow without
bound between restarts and help fill the disk in the first place. Rotate on age
or size at startup, and add a bounded periodic check that rotates the live file
once it passes a size cap (rename plus SonicBoom reopen, the standard logrotate
pattern), capping on-disk logs at roughly two files.

* fix(server): keep the stderr fallback from crashing on async write errors

The destination guard writes to process.stderr inside a try/catch, but a stderr
write can fail asynchronously (EPIPE when its reader closed the pipe); that
'error' event escapes the try/catch and, with no listener on stderr, would crash
the process the guard exists to protect. Register a one-time no-op error listener
on stderr so that failure stays non-fatal.

commit.message:
feat(server): cap Sentry events per issue with a rolling budget (#2724)

* feat(server): cap Sentry events per issue with a rolling budget

A single looping error (a retry loop, a full disk, a missing table hit on
every request) currently emits one Sentry event per failure with no ceiling,
which drains the org's error quota and drops legitimate events from other
issues. beforeSend now runs each event through a per-issue budget that admits a
handful of representative events per rolling window and drops the rest, tagging
the next admitted event with how many were suppressed. The budget is in-memory
and keyed to match Sentry grouping, so it needs no external state.

* fix(server): make the event budget window rolling and its key per-issue

Address two review findings on the per-issue Sentry budget:

- The window was fixed, not rolling: resetting the counter on the boundary let
  an issue send nearly twice maxPerKey around the edge. Track admitted
  timestamps and expire each by age so the cap holds over any window-length
  span.
- The fallback key used only exception type plus the innermost function name,
  so two distinct issues thrown from same-named functions in different files
  shared one budget. Key on module, filename, and function across the innermost
  in-app frames instead. The exception message stays out of the key on purpose:
  a message carrying a varying id would otherwise mint a fresh key per event and
  escape the cap.
